title: Pattern Recognition or Medical Knowledge? The Problem with Multiple-Choice Questions in Medicine

paper.other_artifacts: Dataset Hugging Face maximegmd/glianorex (MIT, DOI 10.57967/hf/2344): 976 rows, test split only, fields question / options{A-D} / answer_idx / language (en 488, fr 488) / generator; generated textbooks book-gpt4-{en,fr}.md and book-claude35-{en,fr}.md in glianorex-gen

dependence.note: The core finding (LLMs score ~64% on MCQs about a fictional organ while physicians score 27%) is measured directly on model outputs. LLMs were also the dataset generators (gpt-4-turbo and claude-3-5-sonnet generated textbooks and questions), but the generated data is frozen and released, so only the evaluation arm must be re-run. Item-level original outputs were not released (only accuracies).

claim.statement: Despite the Glianorex being fictional and absent from training data, gpt-4o-2024-05-13 answers the 976 four-option MCQs at 0.74 (EN, GPT-generated items) / 0.72 (EN, Claude-generated) / 0.69 (FR, GPT) / 0.71 (FR, Claude) accuracy, and gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 at 0.65 / 0.69 / 0.68 / 0.68, versus physicians at 27% (chance level) - evidence that MCQ scores reflect pattern recognition and test-taking strategies rather than knowledge (Table 6 / Figure 2; Section 4.2.1).
claim.metric: Accuracy (exact match of the selected letter A-D with answer_idx), reported per language x generator subset; 95% CI = 1.96 x SEM; significance vs a random model by binomial CDF.
claim.original_source: Paper Table 6 (Appendix B; accuracy by language and generator, 2 decimals), Figure 2 (accuracy with 95% CI), Section 4.2.1 (means, physician score). 'derived_*' values are our size-weighted averages of Table 6 cells (264/224 items) and are approximations, not published numbers.

protocol.model: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 (primary live arm) and gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 (second live arm)
protocol.model_usage_verified: yes - Table 1 lists gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 and gpt-4o-2024-05-13 as evaluated models; glianorex-oai/main.py instantiates models.OpenAI('gpt-4-turbo') [undated alias, which resolved to 2024-04-09 in mid-2024] and models.OpenAI('gpt-4o-2024-05-13'); re-execution must pin gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 explicitly
protocol.endpoint: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions (original through the `guidance` library's OpenAI backend; guidance[openai] unpinned in requirements.txt)
protocol.prompt_source: glianorex-oai/main.py compute(); dataset loaded with datasets.load_dataset('maximegmd/glianorex', split='test')

params.max_tokens: not set (guidance select emits a single option token)
params.answer_selection: guidance `select` over the four letters after the assistant prefix 'Answer: ' - for remote OpenAI chat models this is realised by generation plus matching, not by prompt log-likelihood; the open-weight models were instead scored by log-likelihood in lm-evaluation-harness (MedQA 4-option format). The exact guidance version used is not pinned (needs user check).

protocol.evaluation: Automatic: acc = 1 if selected letter == answer_idx; accuracy per language (en / fr) and, for Table 6, per generator column; 95% CI = 1.96 x SEM. No logprobs required for the OpenAI arms.
protocol.environment: Python, datasets, guidance[openai] (or a plain openai-SDK re-implementation of the same messages with max_tokens=1-3 and a letter parser)

budget.assumptions: 976 items x 2 models x 3 seeds; ~300 input tokens per call (question 134-1,320 chars + 4 options + instruction), ~4 output tokens. gpt-4-turbo ~$9, gpt-4o ~$5. Temperature 0, so seeds mainly capture API nondeterminism; the ANALYSIS_PLAN paraphrase variants would double this.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1. Primary number: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 overall accuracy on the 976 items (compare to derived 0.715 and to the per-cell Table 6 values). Survival = re-run accuracy (median of 3 seeds) within the bootstrap 95% CI over items of the original (n=976, CI about +/-2.8 pp) AND the behavioral direction holds: accuracy far above chance (25%) and above the physicians' 27% (binomial test p<0.001). Partial = level shifts beyond the CI but stays significantly above chance. Death = accuracy no longer significantly above chance (the paper's thesis would be undermined by a model that refuses/guesses).
judgment.notes: The claim is about behavior on unanswerable-by-knowledge items, so an INCREASE in accuracy also counts as survival of direction. Secondary checks: EN > FR gap (65.7 vs 61.8 across models) and gpt-4o > gpt-4-turbo ordering (Table 7 significance).

domain_notes: All items concern a fictional gland (Glianorex) with invented hormones, receptors and diseases; physicians could not exceed chance, so any above-chance score reflects surface cues (option specificity, exam-style construction) rather than medical knowledge. Both generators (gpt-4-turbo, claude-3-5-sonnet) produced 4-option USMLE-style vignettes at temperature 1; 4 EN and 4 FR items are known to be incomplete (<1%). Successor models may have seen the public HF dataset (released 2024), which would inflate rather than deflate their scores - the authors recommend regenerating a private variant with glianorex-gen for contamination-free successor arms.
decisions_2026_09_18: one card, two rows: primary gpt-4o-2024-05-13 (Table 6), second gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09
